questions.question: A woman travelled at a speed of 20 m/min for 90 min, and at a speed of 55 m/min for 60 min. Her average speed (in m/min) for the entire journey is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Time ratio = 90 : 60 = 3 : 2

⇒ Average speed = (20 × 3 + 55 × 2) ÷ (3 + 2)

⇒ = (60 + 110) ÷ 5 = 170 ÷ 5 = 34

**∴ Answer = 34 m/min**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Speed₁ = 20 m/min, Time₁ = 90 min

⇒ Speed₂ = 55 m/min, Time₂ = 60 min

**Formula:**

⇒ Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance₁ = 20 × 90 = 1800 m

⇒ Distance₂ = 55 × 60 = 3300 m

⇒ Total Distance = 1800 + 3300 = 5100 m

⇒ Total Time = 90 + 60 = 150 min

⇒ Average Speed = 5100 ÷ 150 = 34 m/min

**Final Answer: 34 m/min**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Average Speed (Different Times):** When time is different, use weighted average → (v₁t₁ + v₂t₂) ÷ (t₁ + t₂)

**2. Average Speed (Equal Distances):** Use harmonic mean → 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂)

**3. Shortcut Concept:** If time ratio is given, multiply speeds with time ratio directly

questions.question: The Lilatilakam, a 14th-century treatise, played a significant role in establishing the classical status of which Indian language through its grammatical and poetic principles?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Malayalam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lilatilakam** is a **14th-century** treatise written in **Sanskrit** that deals with the grammar and poetics of **Mani-pravalam**, a literary style used in medieval **Kerala**.
 
• The text is considered the earliest known grammatical work on the **Malayalam** language, providing crucial evidence for its evolution as a distinct identity from **Tamil** and **Sanskrit**.
 
• It defines **Mani-pravalam** as the "union of **Manipravalam** (Ruby and Coral)," where **Mani** represents **Sanskrit** and **Pravalam** represents the regional language, **Malayalam**.
 
• The treatise consists of **eight Silpas** (chapters) covering various aspects of linguistic structure, including parts of speech, syntax, and poetic figures of speech.
 
• By standardizing grammatical principles and poetic rules, **Lilatilakam** laid the foundation for the recognition of **Malayalam** as a classical and sophisticated literary language.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Classical Languages of India:**

 
 
• The **Government of India** officially grants "Classical Status" to languages that have high antiquity, a rich heritage of ancient literature, and an original literary tradition.
 
• **Tamil** was the first language to be declared a classical language in **2004**, followed by **Sanskrit** in **2005**.
 
• **Kannada** and **Telugu** were added to the list in **2008**.
 
• **Malayalam** was officially recognized as a classical language in **2013**, largely due to its historical roots evidenced in texts like **Lilatilakam** and its **Chera** dynasty connections.
 
• **Odia** became the sixth classical language in **2014**. In **2024**, the **Union Cabinet** approved five more: **Marathi**, **Pali**, **Prakrit**, **Assamese**, and **Bengali**.
 
 
 
• **Kannada:** An ancient Dravidian language primarily spoken in **Karnataka**, with its earliest literature dating back to the **Kavirajamarga** in the **9th century**.
 
• **Tamil:** One of the oldest surviving classical languages, with the **Sangam literature** dating back to **300 BCE** to **300 CE**.
 
• **Odia:** Predominantly spoken in **Odisha**, it has a rich history of inscriptions and literature like the **Mahabharata** by **Sarala Das** in the **15th century**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **Mani-pravalam** literally translates to **diamonds and corals**, symbolizing the aesthetic blending of two different languages to create a unique literary form.
 
• **Lilatilakam** is historically significant because it identifies the **Malayalam** of the **Chera** kingdom (specifically the **Kerala** region) as a language independent of **Tamil** by the **14th century**.
 
• The **Malayalam** alphabet is largely derived from the **Grantha script**, which was used for writing **Sanskrit** in **South India**.
 
• The establishment of **Malayalam** as a classical language requires that its early texts, like the **Ramacharitam** and **Lilatilakam**, demonstrate a tradition spanning over **1500 to 2000 years**.

questions.question: {If } (a + (1)/(a)) = 4, { then what is the value of } (a⁵ + (1)/(a⁵⁾)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use identity pattern:

a + 1/a = 4

⇒ a² + 1/a² = 4² − 2 = 16 − 2 = 14

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 4 × 14 − 4 = 56 − 4 = 52

⇒ a⁵ + 1/a⁵ = (a² + 1/a²)(a³ + 1/a³) − (a + 1/a)

⇒ = (14 × 52) − 4 = 728 − 4 = 724

**∴ Answer = 724**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ a + 1/a = 4

**Formula:**

⇒ aⁿ + 1/aⁿ formed using recurrence:

aⁿ + 1/aⁿ = (a + 1/a)(aⁿ−¹ + 1/aⁿ−¹) − (aⁿ−² + 1/aⁿ−²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ a² + 1/a² = 4 × 4 − 2 = 16 − 2 = 14

⇒ a³ + 1/a³ = 4 × 14 − 4 = 56 − 4 = 52

⇒ a⁴ + 1/a⁴ = 4 × 52 − 14 = 208 − 14 = 194

⇒ a⁵ + 1/a⁵ = 4 × 194 − 52 = 776 − 52 = 724

**Final Answer: 724**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Basic Identity:** a² + 1/a² = (a + 1/a)² − 2

**2. Cubic Identity:** a³ + 1/a³ = (a + 1/a)³ − 3(a + 1/a)

**3. Recurrence Relation:** Tₙ = (a + 1/a)Tₙ−₁ − Tₙ−₂

**4. Exam Tip:** Always build values stepwise instead of expanding high powers directly

questions.question: Which of the following scientists gave the concept of atomic mass?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Dalton**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **John Dalton** was an **English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist** who is best known for introducing the **Atomic Theory** into chemistry in the year **1808**.
 
• He was the first scientist to provide a logical explanation for the **atomic mass** of elements. He proposed that every **element** consists of tiny, indivisible particles called **atoms**, and that all atoms of a specific element have a **constant mass** that distinguishes them from atoms of other elements.
 
• In his seminal work, **"A New System of Chemical Philosophy"**, Dalton published the first table of **relative atomic weights**. He used **Hydrogen** as the standard reference point, assigning it an **atomic mass of 1**, because it was the lightest element known at the time.
 
• His theory stated that **chemical reactions** involve the rearrangement of atoms and that atoms combine in simple **numerical ratios** to form compounds. The concept of **atomic mass** was essential to explain the **Law of Definite Proportions** and the **Law of Multiple Proportions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ernest Rutherford (1871–1937):**

 
 
• A **New Zealand-born British physicist** who is widely regarded as the **father of nuclear physics**.
 
• In **1911**, he performed the famous **Gold Foil Experiment** (Alpha-particle scattering experiment), which led to the discovery of the **atomic nucleus**.
 
• He postulated that the **mass of an atom** is concentrated in a tiny, positively charged **nucleus** at the center, rather than being distributed throughout the atom.
 
 
 
• **J.J. Thomson (1856–1940):**
 
 
• An **English physicist** who revolutionized the understanding of atomic structure by discovering the **electron** in **1897**.
 
• He used **cathode ray tube** experiments to show that atoms contain negatively charged subatomic particles.
 
• He proposed the **"Plum Pudding Model"** of the atom, where the atom was envisioned as a sphere of positive charge with **electrons** embedded in it like raisins in a pudding.
 
 
 
• **Niels Bohr (1885–1962):**
 
 
• A **Danish physicist** who proposed the **Bohr Model** of the atom in **1913**.
 
• He improved upon Rutherford's model by suggesting that **electrons** move in fixed **circular orbits** or **energy levels** around the nucleus.
 
• His work incorporated **quantum theory** to explain how electrons can have stable orbits and why atoms emit specific spectra of light.
 
 
 
• **Modern Concept of Atomic Mass:**
 
 
• Today, the **Unified Atomic Mass Unit (u)** is used, which is defined as **1/12th** of the mass of an unbound neutral atom of **Carbon-12** at its nuclear and electronic ground state.
 
• The **relative atomic mass** is a dimensionless physical quantity, representing the ratio of the average mass of atoms of a chemical element in a given sample to the **atomic mass constant**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• While **John Dalton** correctly identified that atoms have mass, modern science has discovered **isotopes**—atoms of the same element that have **different masses** due to a different number of **neutrons**.
 
• The **Atomic Number** (number of protons), which defines the identity of an element, was a later discovery (by **Henry Moseley** in **1913**), whereas Dalton focused strictly on **atomic weight**.
 
• Dalton's **atomic theory** provided the quantitative basis for chemistry, transforming it from a qualitative study into a precise **mathematical science**.

questions.question: Which Himalayan region has greater altitudinal variations?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eastern Himalayan region**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Eastern Himalayan region** is known for having greater **altitudinal variations** compared to the Western Himalayas. This is primarily because the mountains in the east rise very **abruptly** from the plains of **Assam** and **West Bengal**.
 
• Due to the sudden rise in height, the **vertical zonation** of vegetation is much more compressed and varied, leading to a rapid transition from **tropical forests** at the foothills to **alpine meadows** at higher elevations.
 
• The region includes the states of **Arunachal Pradesh**, **Sikkim**, and the hills of **West Bengal**, along with neighboring countries like **Bhutan**.
 
• The proximity of the **Eastern Himalayas** to the **Bay of Bengal** ensures that it receives heavy **monsoon rainfall**, which further enhances the biological and climatic diversity across different altitudes.
 
• In contrast, the **Western Himalayas** rise more gradually through a series of ranges like the **Shiwaliks** and **Himachal**, resulting in less dramatic altitudinal shifts over short horizontal distances.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Western Himalayan Region:**

 
 
• This region spans across **Jammu and Kashmir**, **Ladakh**, **Himachal Pradesh**, and **Uttarakhand**.
 
• It is characterized by a **greater width**, reaching up to **400 km** in some areas, whereas the Eastern section is narrower (approx **150 km**).
 
• The **Western Himalayas** are generally drier, with precipitation occurring mostly in the **winter** due to **Western Disturbances**.
 
 
 
• **Vegetation and Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The **Eastern Himalayas** are recognized as a **Global Biodiversity Hotspot**. It is home to unique species such as the **Red Panda** and thousands of varieties of **Orchids** and **Rhododendrons**.
 
• The **Western Himalayas** are dominated by **temperate coniferous forests** featuring trees like **Deodar**, **Blue Pine**, and **Silver Fir**.
 
 
 
• **Snowline Differences:**
 
 
• The **snowline** (the altitude above which snow remains all year) is higher in the **Eastern Himalayas** (around **4,400 to 4,500 meters**) because of higher **humidity** and lower **latitudes**.
 
• In the **Western Himalayas**, the snowline is lower, found at approximately **2,500 to 3,000 meters** on the southern slopes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Highest Peaks:** The **Eastern Himalayan region** houses **Kanchenjunga**, the highest peak in **India** at **8,586 meters**, located in **Sikkim**.
 
• **Rainfall Data:** The **Eastern Himalayas** receive more than **200 cm** of annual rainfall, making them significantly more humid than the Western counterparts which receive roughly **100 cm** or less in many parts.
 
• **River Systems:** The **Brahmaputra** is the primary river system of the **Eastern Himalayas**, while the **Indus**, **Jhelum**, **Chenab**, **Ravi**, and **Beas** originate or flow through the **Western Himalayas**.
 
• **Geological Fact:** The **Himalayas** are **Young Fold Mountains**, formed by the collision of the **Indo-Australian Plate** and the **Eurasian Plate** during the **Cenozoic Era**.

questions.question: A student wants to locate a word inside a PDF. Which shortcut helps?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + F**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + F**: This keyboard shortcut is the standard command for the **"Find"** function across almost all **operating systems** and applications. When a student presses this in a **PDF reader** (like **Adobe Acrobat** or a **web browser**), a search bar appears, allowing them to type and **locate specific words** or phrases within the document. *Hence, this option is correct.*
 
• **Ctrl + V**: This shortcut is used for the **Paste** function. It allows a user to insert content that has been previously **copied** or **cut** into the current cursor location or selected area. It does not provide any search or location functionality. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Ctrl + Tab**: This is a **navigation shortcut** used to switch between different **tabs** within a single window, such as in **Google Chrome**, **Mozilla Firefox**, or **Microsoft Edge**. It moves the focus to the next tab to the right but does not search for text. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Ctrl + C**: This is the command for **Copy**. It places the selected text, image, or file into the system **clipboard** so it can be moved or duplicated elsewhere. While it helps in selecting text, it cannot search for words inside a **PDF**. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PDF Navigation and Tools**: **Portable Document Format (PDF)** files are widely used because they maintain **formatting** across different devices. To navigate them efficiently, shortcuts like **Ctrl + G** (Go to page) or **Ctrl + Home** (Go to start) are often used alongside **Ctrl + F**.
 
• **Cross-Platform Consistency**: Keyboard shortcuts are designed for **efficiency** and **ergonomics**. In **macOS**, the equivalent of the **Control (Ctrl)** key is the **Command (Cmd)** key. Therefore, to find a word on a **Mac**, a user would press **Cmd + F**.
 
• **Advanced Search Features**: Most **PDF readers** provide advanced "Find" options such as **Case Sensitivity** (matching capital letters exactly), **Whole Words Only** (to avoid finding parts of larger words), and **Find Previous/Next** using **Enter** or **Shift + Enter**.
 
• **History of Shortcuts**: Many modern shortcuts were popularized by **Xerox PARC** and later adopted by **Apple** and **Microsoft** in the **1980s**. The **"F"** in **Ctrl + F** stands for **"Find"**, making it a **mnemonic** shortcut that is easy for users to remember.
 
• **Browser Integration**: Since many students open **PDFs** directly in **web browsers**, **Ctrl + F** works identically in browsers like **Chrome** and **Safari** to highlight every instance of the searched term in the **visible text**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Universal Shortcuts**: Some of the most common **Windows** shortcuts include **Ctrl + S** for **Save**, **Ctrl + P** for **Print**, **Ctrl + Z** for **Undo**, and **Ctrl + A** for **Select All**. These are vital for **digital literacy** and **productivity**.
 
• **OCR Limitations**: If a **PDF** is a **scanned image** rather than a text-based file, **Ctrl + F** might not work unless the file has undergone **Optical Character Recognition (OCR)**. **OCR** technology converts images of typed text into **machine-encoded text** that can be searched.
 
• **Selection vs. Search**: While **Ctrl + C** and **Ctrl + V** are part of the **"Copy-Paste"** workflow, they are independent of the **"Search"** workflow triggered by **Ctrl + F**.
 
• **Application Variety**: In **Excel**, **Ctrl + F** opens a dialog box that allows searching across **Worksheets** or **Workbooks**, demonstrating its versatility beyond just **PDFs**.

questions.question: Cheriyal scroll painting belongs to which State of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telangana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cheriyal Scroll Painting** is a highly stylized and unique version of **Nakashi art**, which is native to the state of **Telangana** in **India**.
 
• This traditional art form originated in the **Cheriyal** village, located in the **Siddipet district** of **Telangana**, and has been practiced for several centuries.
 
• The paintings are primarily used as a tool for **storytelling**. These **scrolls** serve as visual aids for traditional balladeers who travel from village to village, narrating stories from **Indian Mythology**, the **Puranas**, and the **Epics** like the **Ramayana** and **Mahabharata**.
 
• In recognition of its unique cultural value and specific geographical origin, **Cheriyal Scroll Painting** was awarded the **Geographical Indication (GI)** tag in the year **2007**.
 
• The canvas for these paintings is traditionally prepared using **khadi cloth**, which is treated with a specialized paste made from **tamarind seeds**, **white mud**, and **rice starch** to ensure the longevity and texture of the **Patam** (scroll).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The artisans use **natural colors** extracted from various organic sources; for instance, **white** is obtained from ground sea shells, **black** from **lamp soot**, **yellow** from **turmeric**, and **blue** from the **indigo** plant.
 
• A distinctive feature of **Cheriyal paintings** is the **red background**, which makes the figures and narratives stand out prominently. The characters are usually depicted in **profile** with **sharp features** and large, expressive eyes.
 
• The **Kaki Padagollu** community is the primary group of storytellers associated with these scrolls, using them to perform **folklore** and mythological dramas for rural audiences.
 
• Beyond the large scrolls, which could historically reach **40 to 45 feet** in length, modern artisans also create **Cheriyal masks** and **dolls**. These are made from **sawdust** and **tamarind paste** and often represent various deities or characters from rural life.
 
• Other notable **GI-tagged** crafts from **Telangana** include **Pochampally Ikat**, **Silver Filigree of Karimnagar**, **Pembarthi Metal Craft**, and **Bidriware** from **Hyderabad**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• While **scroll paintings** are found in other parts of **India**, such as **Pattachitra** in **Odisha** and **Phad paintings** in **Rajasthan**, the **Cheriyal** style is unique due to its specific **iconography** and the influence of **Deccani** artistic traditions.
 
• In the past, each community had its own set of scrolls; for example, the **Madiga** community had **Goud Purana** scrolls, and the **Mala** community had **Markandeya Purana** scrolls, showing the deep link between the art and the social fabric of **Telangana**.
 
• Due to modernization and the decline of traditional storytelling, the **scrolls** have been scaled down in size. Today, they are often produced as **1-foot to 3-foot** panels intended for **interior decoration** and **souvenirs** to preserve the heritage.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

30% of 80 = 24

⇒ √³729 = 9 and √49 = 7

⇒ Expression = 24 − (4/7 × 9 × 7)

⇒ 7 cancels ⇒ 4 × 9 = 36

⇒ 24 − 36 = −12

**∴ Answer = −12**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ y = 30% of 80 − (4/7 × √³729 × √49)

**Formula:**

⇒ Percentage: x% of y = (x/100) × y

**Calculations:**

⇒ 30% of 80 = (30/100) × 80 = 24

⇒ √³729 = 9

⇒ √49 = 7

⇒ 4/7 × 9 × 7 = 4 × 9 = 36

⇒ y = 24 − 36 = −12

**Final Answer: −12**

**1. Percentage Trick:** 30% = 3/10, so multiply directly for faster calculation

**2. Cube Root Concept:** √³a³ = a

**3. Square Root Concept:** √a² = a

**4. Simplification Tip:** Always simplify roots first to reduce calculation time

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

∠AEF = Corresponding ∠CFt (external) = 70°.

∠GEF = ∠AEF ÷ 2 = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°.

∠EFG = 180° − (70° + 25°) = 85°.

∠EGF = 180° − (35° + 85°) = 180° − 120° = 60°.

**∴ Answer = 60°**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

AB || CD, Transversal t. EG bisects ∠AEF. ∠CFG = 25°, ∠CFt (lower angle) = 70°.

**Formula used:**

1. Corresponding angles are equal for parallel lines.

2. Linear pair angles sum to 180°.

3. Angle Sum Property of a triangle = 180°.

 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• AB CD EF G t 70° 25° x° 

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Find ∠AEF.

⇒ ∠AEF and ∠CFt (70°) are corresponding angles.

⇒ ∠AEF = 70°

Step 2: Find ∠GEF.

⇒ EG is the bisector of ∠AEF.

⇒ ∠GEF = 70° ÷ 2 = 35°

Step 3: Find ∠EFG.

⇒ ∠CFE + ∠CFt = 180° (Linear pair)

⇒ ∠CFE = 180° − 70° = 110°

⇒ ∠EFG = ∠CFE − ∠CFG = 110° − 25° = 85°

Step 4: Find ∠EGF (x).

⇒ In ΔEGF, ∠EGF + ∠GEF + ∠EFG = 180°

⇒ x + 35° + 85° = 180°

⇒ x + 120° = 180°

⇒ x = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Alternative Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternative interior angles (like ∠AEF and ∠EFD) are equal.

Consecutive Interior Angles

Angles on the same side of the transversal between parallel lines (like ∠BEF and ∠EFD) sum to 180°.

Vertically Opposite Angles

Angles opposite each other at a vertex where two lines cross are always equal.

External Angle of Triangle

An exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the two opposite interior angles.

questions.question: The state of matter where particles are far apart and move randomly and quickly is the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gaseous state**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gaseous state** is characterized by particles that have very **weak intermolecular forces** of attraction, allowing them to stay **far apart** from one another. *Hence, the statement about particles being far apart is correct.*
 
• Particles in a **gas** possess high **Kinetic Energy**, which causes them to move **randomly and quickly** in all possible directions. *Hence, the statement about random and quick movement is correct.*
 
• Because of the large **intermolecular spaces**, gases do not have a **fixed shape** or a **fixed volume**; they expand to completely fill the **container** they are placed in.
 
• This state of matter is highly **compressible** compared to **solids** and **liquids**, as the **empty space** between particles can be reduced significantly under **pressure**.
 
• The constant, **random motion** of gas particles leads to a phenomenon known as **diffusion**, where gases mix evenly with one another regardless of their **densities**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solid State:**

 
 
• In a **solid**, particles are **tightly packed** in a regular pattern called a **lattice**.
 
• The **intermolecular forces** are strongest in this state, giving solids a **definite shape** and **definite volume**.
 
• Particles only **vibrate** about their **fixed positions** and do not move **randomly** or **quickly** across distances.
 
 
 
• **Liquid State:**
 
 
• In a **liquid**, particles are **close together** but do not have a **fixed arrangement**.
 
• Liquids have a **fixed volume** but take the **shape of the container** because particles can **slide past** each other.
 
• The **kinetic energy** of liquid particles is higher than in solids but lower than in **gases**.
 
 
 
• **Plasma State:**
 
 
• **Plasma** is considered the **fourth state of matter**, consisting of **super-heated**, **ionized gas**.
 
• It contains **electrons** and **positive ions** that move at **extremely high speeds**, making it highly **conductive** to electricity.
 
• It is the most **abundant** state of matter in the **universe**, found in **stars** (including the **Sun**) and **neon signs**.
 
 
 
• **Bose-Einstein Condensate (BEC):**
 
 
• This is the **fifth state of matter** formed when a **gas** of **bosons** is cooled to temperatures very close to **absolute zero** (**0 Kelvin** or **-273.15°C**).
 
• In this state, **atoms** lose their **individual identity** and behave as a **single quantum entity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Brownian Motion:** This refers to the **erratic, zigzag motion** of microscopic particles suspended in a **fluid** (liquid or gas) resulting from their **collision** with the fast-moving **atoms or molecules** in the gas or liquid.
 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:** This theory explains that the **pressure** exerted by a **gas** is due to the constant **collisions** of its particles with the **walls of the container**.
 
• **Temperature Effect:** Increasing the **temperature** of a gas increases the **average kinetic energy** of the particles, causing them to move even **faster** and increase the **frequency of collisions**.
 
• **Examples:** Common examples of the **gaseous state** include **Oxygen (O2)**, **Nitrogen (N2)**, **Carbon Dioxide (CO2)**, and **Water Vapor**.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the Baishagu festival celebrated by the Boro Kacharis in the month of April?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Baishagu festival** is the most popular and cherished festival celebrated by the **Boro-Kachari** (also known as **Bodos**) community in the state of **Assam**.
 
• It is traditionally celebrated in the middle of **April**, coinciding with the arrival of the **spring season** and the start of the **Assamese New Year** (**Bohag Bihu**).
 
• The festival is observed on the first day of the month of **Baisakh** (Vaisakha) in the **Hindu calendar**, marking the end of the old year and the beginning of the new harvest cycle.
 
• The primary purpose of **Baishagu** is to offer prayers to **Lord Bathou** (identified as **Lord Shiva**) for peace, harmony, and a prosperous agricultural yield in the coming year.
 
• One of the most distinctive features of this festival is the **Bagurumba dance**, a traditional folk dance performed by **Bodo women**, characterized by graceful movements that resemble the fluttering of butterflies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Boro-Kachari Tribe**: They are the largest ethnic and linguistic community in **Assam**, primarily concentrated in the **Bodoland Territorial Region (BTR)**. They belong to the **Tibeto-Burman** language family and the **Indo-Mongoloid** group.
 
• **Ritualistic Practices**: The first day of the festival, known as **Gwra-Gwra**, is dedicated to the worship of **cows**. Cattle are taken to the riverside, washed, and decorated with garlands made of **turmeric** and **vegetables**. The second day, called **Manwi**, involves people visiting relatives, seeking blessings from elders, and enjoying community feasts.
 
• **Musical Instruments**: The celebrations are incomplete without traditional **Bodo** instruments such as the **Sifung** (a long bamboo flute), **Kham** (a traditional drum), **Serja** (a bowed violin-like instrument), and **Jota** (cymbals).
 
• **Traditional Cuisine**: During **Baishagu**, special dishes like **Ondla** (a rice powder curry) and local preparations made from **pork** and **silkworms** are commonly consumed. **Jou** (traditional rice beer) also plays a role in the festivities.
 
• **Religious Context**: While many **Bodos** follow **Bathouism**, which involves the worship of the **Sijou tree** (Euphorbia splendens), the festival is celebrated by all members of the community regardless of their specific religious sects (such as **Brahma Dharma** or **Christianity**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other States**:

 
 
• **Bihar**: Known for festivals like **Chhath Puja** and **Sama Chakeva**. Its New Year is often celebrated as **Jude Sheetal**.
 
• **Karnataka**: Celebrates its New Year as **Ugadi**, typically in **March** or **April**, according to the **Luni-Solar calendar**.
 
• **Odisha**: Observes **Pana Sankranti** (also known as **Maha Bishuba Sankranti**) as the Odia New Year in mid-**April**.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance**: **Baishagu** acts as a platform for **social bonding** and the preservation of **tribal heritage** in the **Northeast** region of **India**. It showcases the deep connection between the **Bodo people** and **nature**.
 
• **Dates and Duration**: While the official holiday is usually **April 14th** or **15th**, the community celebrations can continue for up to a week.

questions.question: What was the primary objective of the 'Blue Skies 2025' campaign launched in August 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Reduce urban air pollution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **'Blue Skies 2025'** campaign was launched in **August 2025** as a renewed national initiative to tackle the growing crisis of **air pollution** in metropolitan and industrial hubs. The primary objective of this campaign is to **Reduce urban air pollution** through localized action plans and technological interventions.
 
• This campaign is an extension of the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)**, aiming to achieve a **35% to 45% reduction** in **Particulate Matter (PM2.5 and PM10)** concentrations by the year **2026-2027**, using **2024-2025** as the new baseline period. Hence, the statement regarding its objective to reduce pollution is correct.
 
• The initiative specifically targets **131 non-attainment cities** across **India** that do not meet the **National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS)**. It focuses on the implementation of **City Specific Action Plans (CSAPs)** to monitor **AQI (Air Quality Index)** in real-time.
 
• Key features of the campaign include the deployment of **Smog Towers**, the expansion of **Mechanical Street Sweepers**, and the integration of **AI-based traffic management** to reduce idling emissions at major intersections.
 
• The campaign is spearheaded by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** in collaboration with the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**. It emphasizes a multi-sectoral approach involving transport, industry, and waste management sectors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP):**

 
 
• Launched in **January 2019**, it was India's first-ever effort to frame a national framework for **air quality management** with a time-bound reduction target.
 
• The **NCAP** initially aimed for a **20% to 30%** reduction in **PM** concentrations by **2024**, which has been evolved under the **Blue Skies 2025** framework to meet more stringent global standards.
 
 
 
• **Air Quality Index (AQI):**
 
 
• The **AQI** is a tool used by government agencies to communicate to the public how polluted the air currently is or how polluted it is forecast to become.
 
• It categorizes air quality into six levels: **Good (0-50)**, **Satisfactory (51-100)**, **Moderately Polluted (101-200)**, **Poor (201-300)**, **Very Poor (301-400)**, and **Severe (401-500)**.
 
 
 
• **Pollutants Monitored:**
 
 
• Under the **NAAQS**, **12 pollutants** are monitored, including **Sulphur Dioxide (SO2)**, **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)**, **Particulate Matter (PM10 and PM2.5)**, **Ozone (O3)**, **Lead (Pb)**, and **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**.
 
• The **Blue Skies 2025** campaign places a heavy emphasis on **Secondary Pollutants** like ground-level **Ozone**, which has become a significant concern during summer months in **India**.
 
 
 
• **International Context:**
 
 
• The campaign aligns with the **United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)** goals and the **International Day of Clean Air for Blue Skies**, celebrated annually on **September 7**.
 
• It contributes to achieving **Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 11** (Sustainable Cities and Communities) and **SDG 3** (Good Health and Well-being).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legislative Framework:** The campaign draws its legal authority from the **Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981** and the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986**. These acts empower the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** to impose fines on **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** that fail to meet **air quality** targets.
 
• **Funding and Scale:** For the fiscal year **2025-2026**, a budget of **₹2,500 crore** was allocated for **air quality improvement** in **42 cities** with a population of more than **one million**, under the recommendation of the **15th Finance Commission**.
 
• **Technological Integration:** The campaign promotes the **PRANA (Portal for Regulation of Air-pollution in Non-Attainment cities)** portal, which serves as a centralized platform for monitoring the physical and financial status of city action plans.
 
• **Geographical Focus:** While the campaign is national, special focus is given to the **Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP)**, where topography and meteorological factors often lead to the trapping of **pollutants** during the **winter season**.

questions.question: Mr. ABCD wants to become a member of the Legislative Assembly. What is the minimum age prescribed in the Constitution of India so that he becomes a member of the Legislative Assembly?

options.text: No Minimum age is prescribed in the Constitution

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**25 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Article 173** of the **Constitution of India**, a person must be at least **25 years** of age to become a member of the **Legislative Assembly** (Vidhan Sabha).
 
• The candidate must be a **citizen of India** and must make and subscribe before some person authorized in that behalf by the **Election Commission** an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the **Third Schedule**.
 
• For the **Legislative Council** (Vidhan Parishad) of a state, the minimum age prescribed is **30 years**, similar to the **Rajya Sabha** at the central level.
 
• The **Legislative Assembly** is the lower house (in states with a bicameral legislature) or the sole house (in states with a unicameral legislature) of the state legislature in **India**.
 
• The members of the **Legislative Assembly** are directly elected by the people on the basis of **adult suffrage** from territorial constituencies within the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Age Requirements for Various Constitutional Posts:**

 
 
• **President of India**: The minimum age required to contest the election for the **President** is **35 years** (under **Article 58**).
 
• **Vice-President of India**: The minimum age required is **35 years** (under **Article 66**).
 
• **Governor of a State**: A person must have completed the age of **35 years** to be appointed as a **Governor** (under **Article 157**).
 
• **Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha)**: The minimum age is **25 years**, same as the **Legislative Assembly**.
 
• **Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha)**: The minimum age is **30 years**.
 
• **Panchayats and Municipalities**: For contesting elections to **local bodies** like **Panchayats** and **Municipalities**, the minimum age is **21 years** (under **Article 243F** and **Article 243V**).
 
 
 
• **Voting Age in India**:
 
 
• The **61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988** lowered the voting age from **21 years** to **18 years** for both **Lok Sabha** and **State Legislative Assembly** elections. This came into force in **1989**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disqualifications for Membership:**

 
 
• A person can be disqualified from being a member of the **Legislative Assembly** if they hold any **office of profit** under the **Government of India** or the Government of any State.
 
• If the person is of **unsound mind** and stands so declared by a competent court, or is an undischarged **insolvent**.
 
• If the person is not a **citizen of India**, or has voluntarily acquired the citizenship of a foreign State.
 
 
 
• **Term of the Legislative Assembly:**
 
 
• The normal term of every **Legislative Assembly** is **5 years** from the date appointed for its first meeting, unless dissolved earlier by the **Governor**.
 
• During a **Proclamation of Emergency**, this period may be extended by **Parliament** by law for a period not exceeding **one year** at a time.
 
 
 
• **Representation of People Act, 1951**:
 
 
• Besides constitutional provisions, a person must possess such other qualifications as may be prescribed by **Parliament**. Under the **Representation of People Act, 1951**, a person must be an **elector** for any assembly constituency in that state to contest for the **Legislative Assembly**.

questions.question: The price of each article of type P, Q, and R is ₹280, ₹180 and ₹115, respectively. Tejas buys articles of each type in the ratio 4 : 2 : 5 for ₹6,165. How many articles of type Q did he purchase?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 2 : 5 → Let units = 4x, 2x, 5x

⇒ Total cost per x = (4×280 + 2×180 + 5×115)

⇒ = 1120 + 360 + 575 = 2055

⇒ Total = 6165 ⇒ x = 6165 ÷ 2055 = 3

⇒ Q articles = 2x = 6

**∴ Answer = 6**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Price of P = 280

⇒ Price of Q = 180

⇒ Price of R = 115

⇒ Ratio = 4 : 2 : 5

⇒ Total cost = 6165

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let number of articles = 4x, 2x, 5x

⇒ Total cost = 4x×280 + 2x×180 + 5x×115

⇒ = 1120x + 360x + 575x

⇒ = 2055x

⇒ 2055x = 6165

⇒ x = 6165 ÷ 2055 = 3

⇒ Number of Q = 2x = 6

**∴ Final Answer: 6**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Ratio Concept:** If ratio is a:b:c → quantities = ax, bx, cx

**2. Total Cost:** Sum of (quantity × price)

**3. Unit Method:** First find cost per unit ratio, then scale

**4. Shortcut Tip:** Always combine ratio with prices first

questions.question: Which island country, along with Sri Lanka, is identified as India’s southern neighbour across the Indian Ocean?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maldives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maldives** is an island country located in the **Indian Ocean**, situated to the **south-west** of the Indian mainland. It is officially known as the **Republic of Maldives** and consists of a double chain of **26 atolls**.
 
• Along with **Sri Lanka**, it is identified as one of India's two primary southern neighbours across the **Indian Ocean**. While **Sri Lanka** is separated from India by the **Palk Strait**, the **Maldives** is separated from the Indian island of **Minicoy** (part of **Lakshadweep**) by the **Eight Degree Channel**.
 
• The **geographical location** of the **Maldives** is of immense strategic importance to India for maintaining **maritime security** and stability in the **Indian Ocean Region (IOR)**.
 
• The country is composed of approximately **1,192 coral islands**, though only about **200** of these are inhabited. It is the smallest **Asian country** by both **land area** (approx. **298 square kilometers**) and **population**.
 
• In the context of the question, **Maldives** is the correct option as it specifically fits the description of a southern maritime neighbor alongside **Sri Lanka**. ***Hence, the option Maldives is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sri Lanka:** It is an island nation located in **South Asia**, separated from the **Indian subcontinent** by the **Gulf of Mannar** and the **Palk Strait**. Its **location** is just off the southern tip of **India**, making it the closest maritime neighbor.
 
• **Thailand:** This country is located in **Southeast Asia**. While India and **Thailand** share a maritime boundary in the **Andaman Sea**, it is positioned to the **east** of India rather than being a direct southern neighbor across the **Indian Ocean** mainland. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Indonesia:** It is a massive archipelago in **Southeast Asia** and **Oceania**. India shares a maritime border with **Indonesia** at the **Great Channel** (or **Six Degree Channel**), which separates **Indira Point** in the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands** from **Aceh** in **Sumatra**. However, it is generally categorized as a neighbor to the **south-east**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Bhutan:** It is a **landlocked country** in the **Eastern Himalayas**, bordered by **India** to the south, east, and west, and **China** to the north. Since it has no coastline and is located to the **north** of India, it cannot be a southern neighbor across the **Indian Ocean**. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Malé:** It is the **capital** and most populous city of the **Maldives**, located on the southern edge of the **North Malé Atoll**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eight Degree Channel:** This is the **maritime boundary** that separates the **Maldives** from India's **Minicoy Island**. It is so named because it lies on the **8-degree north latitude**.
 
• **Nine Degree Channel:** This channel separates the **island of Minicoy** from the rest of the **Lakshadweep** islands.
 
• **Ten Degree Channel:** This body of water separates the **Andaman Islands** from the **Nicobar Islands** in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
• **Historical Ties:** India was one of the first countries to recognize the **Maldives** after its **independence** in **1965** and established diplomatic relations in **1966**.
 
• **Operation Cactus:** In **1988**, India provided military assistance to the **Maldives** government to thwart a **coup attempt**, further cementing the **security partnership** between the two nations.
 
• **International Memberships:** **Maldives** is a member of the **United Nations (UN)**, the **Commonwealth**, and the **South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)**.

questions.question: During a sale 50% of the goods are sold at 16% profit, 40% of the remaining goods are sold at 35% profit and the still remaining goods are sold at a loss of 25%. If there is an overall profit of x%, then what is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Assume total goods = 100 units

⇒ 50 sold at +16% → weight = 50

⇒ Remaining = 50 → 40% of 50 = 20 sold at +35%

⇒ Remaining = 30 sold at −25%

questions.question: The census in India is conducted once in ten years under the legal authority of the Census Act ____________.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Census Act** was enacted in the year **1948** to provide for certain matters relating to the taking of the census. It provides the legal framework for the decennial census in **India**.
 
• The responsibility of conducting the decennial census rests with the **Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner**, which comes under the **Ministry of Home Affairs**, Government of India.
 
• The **Census Act, 1948** ensures the **confidentiality** of the data collected. According to the act, the information collected from individuals is used only for statistical purposes and cannot be used as evidence in a court of law.
 
• The act empowers the **Central Government** to declare its intention to take a census whenever it may consider it necessary or desirable to do so. Generally, this exercise is conducted every **10 years**.
 
• Under this act, the census officers are appointed to oversee the enumeration process across the **states** and **union territories** of India. It also makes it obligatory for every person to answer the questions asked by the census officers to the best of their knowledge.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background of Census:**

 
 
• The first non-synchronous census in India was conducted in **1872** during the viceroyalty of **Lord Mayo**.
 
• The first synchronous census (conducted simultaneously across the country) took place in **1881** under **Lord Ripon**. Since then, censuses have been undertaken uninterruptedly once every **ten years**.
 
• The **Census of 2011** was the **15th** census of India since **1872** and the **7th** census after independence.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Provision:**
 
 
• The Population Census is a **Union subject** under **Article 246** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• It is listed as **serial number 69** in the **Seventh Schedule** (Union List) of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Census Data:**
 
 
• The data collected serves as the basis for the **delimitation** of constituencies for **Parliament**, **State Legislative Assemblies**, and local bodies.
 
• It is a vital source of information for **policymakers**, **researchers**, and **administrators** to track progress and plan future **socio-economic** developments.

• **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC):**

 
 
• While the regular census is conducted under the **Census Act, 1948**, the **Socio-Economic and Caste Census (SECC)** of **2011** was conducted to identify beneficiaries of government schemes.
 
• Unlike the regular census, where individual data is **confidential**, the data in **SECC** is open for use by government departments to grant or restrict benefits to households.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Hierarchy:**
 
 
• The **Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India** is the highest-ranking officer responsible for the census.
 
• At the state level, the **Director of Census Operations** assists in the execution of the survey.
 
• The **District Collector** or **District Magistrate** acts as the **District Census Officer** to coordinate the work at the local level.

questions.question: Which policy trade-off limited balanced sectoral growth in India during 1951–1991?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Agriculture vs. industry**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The economic strategy of India between **1951** and **1991** was defined by the **Five-Year Plans**, which often faced the fundamental trade-off between **Agriculture** and **Industry**.
 
• During the **First Five-Year Plan (1951–1956)**, the primary focus was on the **Agricultural Sector** to achieve food self-sufficiency and stabilize the economy after **Partition**. This plan was based on the **Harrod-Domar Model**.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)**, drafted by **P.C. Mahalanobis**, shifted the priority drastically toward **Rapid Industrialization** and **Heavy Industries**. This shift created a structural imbalance as resources were diverted from the rural agrarian economy to urban industrial centers.
 
• The trade-off led to a crisis in the **mid-1960s**, where stagnant **agricultural productivity** resulted in severe **food shortages** and a heavy reliance on **PL-480 food aid** from the **USA**.
 
• While **industrialization** was seen as a path to **modernization** and **self-reliance**, the neglect of agriculture limited the internal market's purchasing power, ultimately slowing down the overall **balanced sectoral growth** of the **Indian economy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1956:**

 
 
• This policy formed the basis of the **Second Five-Year Plan** and categorized industries into three schedules, giving the **Public Sector** the "commanding heights" of the economy.
 
• It aimed at **Import Substitution Industrialization (ISI)** to protect domestic industries from foreign competition through high **tariffs** and **quotas**.
 
 
 
• **The Green Revolution (1960s):**
 
 
• To address the **agriculture vs. industry** imbalance, the government introduced **High-Yielding Variety (HYV)** seeds, **chemical fertilizers**, and improved **irrigation**.
 
• This initiative, led by **M.S. Swaminathan**, helped India achieve **food security** but was initially restricted to **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and western **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
 
 
• **Import Substitution vs. Export Promotion:**
 
 
• Between **1951** and **1991**, India followed an **inward-looking trade strategy**. The trade-off here was that by restricting **imports**, Indian industries became inefficient due to lack of **global competition**, and **exports** remained stagnant.
 
 
 
• **The 1991 Economic Reforms:**
 
 
• Due to a **Balance of Payments (BoP)** crisis in **1991**, India moved away from the **License Raj** and adopted **Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization (LPG)**.
 
• This marked the end of the strict **sectoral trade-offs** dictated by **centralized planning**, allowing the **Services Sector** to emerge as a major contributor to the **GDP**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mahalanobis Model:** Focused on **Capital Goods** industries (like steel and machine tools) over **Consumer Goods**, assuming that building a base for heavy industry would lead to long-term **economic growth**.
 
• **Structural Composition:** During this period, the share of **Agriculture** in **GDP** declined, but the percentage of the **workforce** dependent on it did not drop significantly, leading to **disguised unemployment**.
 
• **Role of Public Sector:** The state took the lead in **infrastructure** and **heavy manufacturing**, while the **Private Sector** was heavily regulated through the **MRTP Act (1969)**.

questions.question: The F2 generation of a monohybrid cross typically shows which phenotypic ratio?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3:1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **monohybrid cross** is a genetic cross between two individuals that differ in only one **trait** or **characteristic**. This type of cross was famously used by **Gregor Mendel**, often referred to as the **Father of Genetics**, to understand the patterns of inheritance in **1856-1863**.
 
• The **F2 generation** (Second Filial generation) is produced by the **self-pollination** or selfing of the **F1 generation** (First Filial generation) plants. In Mendel's experiments with the **garden pea** (**Pisum sativum**), the F1 generation always displayed the **dominant phenotype**.
 
• When the F1 hybrids (genotype **Tt**) were crossed with each other, the recessive trait that was hidden in the F1 generation reappeared in the **F2 generation**. The **phenotypic ratio** observed was **3:1**, meaning **75%** of the offspring exhibited the dominant trait and **25%** exhibited the recessive trait.
 
• The **genotypic ratio** of the F2 generation in a monohybrid cross is **1:2:1**, consisting of one **homozygous dominant** (**TT**), two **heterozygous** (**Tt**), and one **homozygous recessive** (**tt**) individual.
 
• This **3:1 ratio** confirms the **Law of Segregation**, which states that allele pairs separate during **gamete formation** and randomly unite at **fertilization**. *Hence, the statement regarding the 3:1 ratio is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Genotype vs. Phenotype:** The **genotype** refers to the actual genetic makeup of an organism (the **alleles** it carries), while the **phenotype** refers to the observable physical **features** or **functions** resulting from those genes, such as **height**, **color**, or **shape**.
 
• **Law of Dominance:** This principle suggests that in a **heterozygous** pair, the **dominant allele** masks the expression of the **recessive allele**. This is why the F1 generation only shows one trait, but the F2 generation shows both in a **3:1** ratio.
 
• **Dihybrid Cross:** If two pairs of contrasting traits are studied simultaneously (e.g., **seed shape** and **seed color**), the F2 phenotypic ratio changes to **9:3:3:1**. This led to Mendel's **Law of Independent Assortment**.
 
• **Punnett Square:** This **statistical tool** was developed by **Reginald C. Punnett** in **1905** to predict the **probability** of offspring inheriting specific **genotypes** and **phenotypes** from a cross.
 
• **Mendel's Selection:** Mendel chose **7 pairs** of contrasting traits in **pea plants**, including **stem height** (Tall/Dwarf), **flower position** (Axial/Terminal), and **seed color** (Yellow/Green), because they were easily identifiable and the plants were easy to **cultivate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Incomplete Dominance:** In some organisms like the **4 o'clock plant** (**Mirabilis jalapa**), the F2 phenotypic ratio is **1:2:1** instead of 3:1, because the **heterozygote** shows an intermediate phenotype (e.g., **Pink flowers** from Red and White parents).
 
• **Test Cross:** This is a cross between an individual of unknown genotype showing a dominant phenotype and a **homozygous recessive** parent. The resulting ratio for a **monohybrid test cross** is **1:1**, which helps determine if the parent is **pure-bred** or **hybrid**.
 
• **Data and Facts:** In one of his **experiments**, Mendel obtained **787 tall** plants and **277 dwarf** plants in the F2 generation, which mathematically approximates the **2.84:1** ratio, rounded to the standard **3:1** ratio.
 
• **Modern Genetics:** While Mendelian ratios are foundational, modern **biology** also explores **polygenic inheritance** and **multiple alleles** (like **ABO blood groups**), where ratios do not follow the simple 3:1 pattern.

questions.question: Who played the most significant military role in leading Nana Sahib's forces during the Revolt of 1857 at Kanpur?

options.text: Bahadur Shah, who appointed Nana Sahib as his Governor
Baji Rao II, the last Peshwa and father of Nana Sahib
Azimullah, who was an expert in political propaganda
Tantia Tope, known for his guerrilla warfare and patriotic resistance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tantia Tope, known for his guerrilla warfare and patriotic resistance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tantia Tope**, whose real name was **Ramachandra Panduranga Yawalkar**, was the most significant military leader and the commander-in-chief of **Nana Sahib's** forces during the **Revolt of 1857**.
 
• He was a loyal associate of **Nana Sahib** and played a pivotal role in the liberation of **Kanpur** from **British** control in **June 1857**.
 
• He is celebrated in Indian history for his mastery of **guerrilla warfare**, which he used effectively to harass **British** troops across **Central India** and the **Bundelkhand** region.
 
• After the fall of **Kanpur**, he continued the struggle alongside **Rani Lakshmibai** of **Jhansi** and successfully captured **Gwalior** in **1858**.
 
• Despite being pursued by several **British** columns, he remained at large for nearly **two years** until he was betrayed by his trusted friend, **Man Singh**, a feudatory of the **Raja of Gwalior**.
 
• He was captured by the **British** in the jungles of **Paron** and was executed at **Shivpuri** on **April 18, 1859**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nana Sahib:**

 
 
• Born as **Dhondu Pant**, he was the adopted son of the last **Maratha Peshwa**, **Baji Rao II**.
 
• The primary grievance of **Nana Sahib** against the **British East India Company** was the refusal to continue his father's pension of **8 lakh rupees** (or **£80,000**) after the **Peshwa's** death in **1851**.
 
• He led the **Revolt of 1857** at **Kanpur** and was proclaimed the **Peshwa** by the rebel sepoys.
 
 
 
• **Azimullah Khan:**
 
 
• He was a sophisticated diplomat and the chief political advisor (**Secretary**) to **Nana Sahib**.
 
• In **1853**, he traveled to **London** to represent **Nana Sahib's** case regarding the pension before the **Board of Control** and the **British Parliament**.
 
• He was instrumental in spreading political propaganda and coordinating with various rebel leaders across **Northern India**.
 
 
 
• **Baji Rao II:**
 
 
• He was the last **Peshwa** of the **Maratha Empire**, reigning from **1795** to **1818**.
 
• After the **Third Anglo-Maratha War**, he was deposed by the **British** and exiled to **Bithoor** near **Kanpur**.
 
 
 
• **Bahadur Shah Zafar:**
 
 
• The last **Mughal Emperor**, he was chosen as the symbolic head and **Shahenshah-e-Hindustan** by the rebel sepoys in **Delhi** in **May 1857**.
 
• Although he gave his blessings to **Nana Sahib** and appointed him as his **Governor** (**Vakil-i-Mutlaq**), his own military authority was largely confined to the **Red Fort**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Siege of Kanpur:** The conflict in **Kanpur** began on **June 4, 1857**, and lasted for **three weeks**. The **British** forces under **General Sir Hugh Wheeler** surrendered on **June 27, 1857**.
 
• **British Suppression:** The **British** forces, led by **General Henry Havelock** and later **Sir Colin Campbell**, eventually recaptured **Kanpur** by **December 1857**.
 
• **Nana Sahib's Fate:** Following the defeat, **Nana Sahib** escaped towards the **Terai** region of **Nepal** in early **1859**. His exact date and place of death remain a subject of historical debate and mystery.
 
• **Significance of Tantia Tope:** His resistance is considered one of the most heroic chapters of the **First War of Indian Independence**, as he managed to keep the flame of rebellion alive long after other major centers like **Delhi** and **Lucknow** had fallen.

questions.question: Article _________ describes the procedure for joint sitting of both Houses of the Parliament in certain cases.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 108**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 108** of the **Constitution of India** provides for the **joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament** (the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha**) in certain cases to resolve a deadlock between them. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 108 is correct.***
 
• A **joint sitting** can be summoned by the **President of India** if a bill passed by one House is rejected by the other House, or if the Houses have finally disagreed as to the amendments to be made in the bill, or if more than **six months** elapse from the date of the reception of the bill by the other House without the bill being passed by it.
 
• The **Speaker of the Lok Sabha** presides over a joint sitting of the two Houses. In the absence of the Speaker, the **Deputy Speaker** of the Lok Sabha presides. If the Deputy Speaker is also absent, the **Deputy Chairman** of the Rajya Sabha presides. Notably, the **Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (the Vice-President of India) does not preside over a joint sitting.
 
• The bill in a joint sitting is passed by a **simple majority** of the total number of members of both Houses present and voting. This usually gives the **Lok Sabha** an advantage due to its larger numerical strength.
 
• It is important to note that the provision of a joint sitting applies only to **Ordinary Bills** and **Financial Bills**. It does not apply to **Money Bills** or **Constitutional Amendment Bills** under **Article 368**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 115**:

 
 
• This article deals with **Supplementary, additional, or excess grants**.
 
• If the amount authorized by any law made in accordance with the provisions of **Article 114** to be expended for a particular service for the current financial year is found to be insufficient, the **President** shall cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament another statement showing the estimated amount of that expenditure.
 
• It ensures that the **Government of India** can seek additional funds if the initial budgetary allocation is exhausted before the end of the **financial year**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 115 is not the correct answer for joint sittings.***
 
 
 
• **Article 104**:
 
 
• This article pertains to the **penalty for sitting and voting** before making an **oath or affirmation** under **Article 99** or when not qualified or when disqualified.
 
• If a person sits or votes as a member of either House of Parliament before he has complied with the requirements of Article 99, he shall be liable in respect of each day on which he so sits or votes to a penalty of **five hundred rupees** to be recovered as a debt due to the **Union**. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 104 is not the correct answer.***
 
 
 
• **Article 94**:
 
 
• This article specifies the **vacation and resignation** of, and removal from, the offices of **Speaker and Deputy Speaker** of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• It states that a member holding office as Speaker or Deputy Speaker shall vacate his office if he ceases to be a member of the **House of the People**.
 
• It also mentions that the Speaker may resign by writing under his hand addressed to the **Deputy Speaker**, and vice-versa. ***Hence, the statement regarding Article 94 is not the correct answer.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In the history of the **Republic of India**, there have been only **three occasions** when a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament was convened to resolve a deadlock:

 
 
• **1961**: For the **Dowry Prohibition Bill**.
 
• **1978**: For the **Banking Service Commission (Repeal) Bill**.
 
• **2002**: For the **Prevention of Terrorism Bill (POTA)**.
 
 
 
• The **Quorum** for a joint sitting is **one-tenth** of the total number of members of both Houses.
 
• The joint sitting is governed by the **Rules of Procedure of Lok Sabha** and not the Rajya Sabha Rules.
 
• Since the **Lok Sabha** has **543** members and the **Rajya Sabha** has **245** members, the will of the Lok Sabha generally prevails in these sessions unless the ruling party in the Lok Sabha has a very slim majority.

questions.question: Who jointly led the first ever no-tax campaign against the British Government in Bengal during the 1838-1848 Farazi Movement?

options.text: Titu Mir and Syed Ahmad Barelvi

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shariatullah Khan and Dadu Mian**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Faraizi Movement** (or Farazi Movement) was initiated by **Haji Shariatullah** in **1818** in **East Bengal** (specifically **Faridpur**). It initially focused on religious reforms but later evolved into a socio-economic struggle.
 
• **Haji Shariatullah** advocated for the fulfillment of **Faraiz** (obligatory duties enjoined by Allah) and encouraged the **peasantry** to protect their rights against the oppression of **Zemindars** and **Indigo planters**.
 
• Following the death of **Haji Shariatullah** in **1840**, his son **Muslihuddin Muhammad Hamam**, popularly known as **Dadu Mian**, took over the leadership and turned the movement into a revolutionary organization between **1838 and 1848**.
 
• **Dadu Mian** organized the first-ever **no-tax campaign** in **Bengal**, urging **farmers** and **peasants** not to pay taxes to **landlords**, whom he considered illegal intermediaries. He proclaimed that "land belongs to **God**," and thus no one had the right to collect taxes on it. ***Hence, the statement regarding Shariatullah Khan and Dadu Mian leading the movement is correct.***
 
• The movement was highly organized; **Dadu Mian** established a parallel government and appointed **Khalifas** (deputies) to look after the interests of the **Faraizis** in different villages, effectively challenging **British authority** and **Zemindari** control.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Haji Shariatullah:** He spent about **20 years** in **Mecca**, where he was influenced by the **Wahhabi** ideology. Upon his return to **India** in **1818**, he aimed to purge **Islam** of **un-Islamic** practices and superstitions that had crept into the **Bengali** Muslim society.
 
• **Dadu Mian's Contributions:** He was a brilliant strategist who divided **East Bengal** into "halqas" (circles) for better administration. Under his leadership, the **Faraizis** formed a **paramilitary force** armed with **clubs** (lathis) to resist the **Zemindars**. He was arrested multiple times by the **British Government** for his rebellious activities and eventually died in **1862**.
 
• **Other Options Context:**
 
 
• **Titu Mir:** He led the **Narkelberia Uprising** (1831) in **West Bengal**. While he also fought against **Zemindars** and **Indigo planters** and was influenced by **Syed Ahmad Barelvi**, he was not the primary leader of the **Faraizi Movement**.
 
• **Syed Ahmad Barelvi:** He was the founder of the **Wahabi Movement** in **India** (centered in **Patna** and the **North-West Frontier Province**), which was distinct from the **Faraizi** movement of **Bengal**.
 
• **Kunwar Singh and Amar Singh:** These were prominent leaders from **Bihar** (Jagdishpur) during the **Great Revolt of 1857**. They were not associated with the **Faraizi** movement of the **1830s**.
 
• **Sidhu Murmu and Kanhu Murmu:** They were the primary leaders of the **Santhal Rebellion** (1855-1856) in the **Rajmahal Hills**, fighting against **British** exploitation and the **Diku** (outsider) system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Faraizi Movement** is considered one of the earliest **agrarian uprisings** in **India** that combined religious fervor with socio-economic grievances.
 
• It specifically targeted the **unholy alliance** between the **British East India Company** and the **local landlords** who exploited the **Muslim** and **Hindu peasantry** alike.
 
• By **1848**, the movement had gained such momentum that the **British** had to take stern military and legal actions to suppress the activities of **Dadu Mian** and his followers.
 
• The movement eventually merged with the broader **Wahabi** sentiment in **India** after the mid-19th century but left a lasting legacy of **peasant resistance** in **Bengal**.

__

questions.question: Which characteristic of a computer system enables it to perform extremely complex calculations within seconds?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Speed** is the fundamental characteristic of a computer that allows it to process **millions of instructions per second (MIPS)**. While a human might take weeks to perform a complex mathematical calculation, a computer can complete it in a **fraction of a second**. ***Hence, the characteristic that enables extremely complex calculations within seconds is Speed.***
 
• The speed of a modern computer is typically measured in **Microseconds (10⁻⁶)**, **Nanoseconds (10⁻⁹)**, and even **Picoseconds (10⁻¹²)**. This high-speed processing is driven by the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, which operates based on a **system clock** measured in **Gigahertz (GHz)**.
 
• In the context of **Supercomputers**, speed is measured in **FLOPS (Floating-Point Operations Per Second)**. For example, as of **2024**, the world's fastest supercomputers operate at **Exascale speeds**, performing more than a **quintillion (10¹⁸)** calculations per second.
 
• This rapid processing is essential for high-end applications such as **weather forecasting**, **nuclear simulations**, **cryptography**, and **complex financial modeling**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Versatility:**

 
 
• **Versatility** refers to the ability of a computer to perform **different types of tasks** simultaneously or sequentially. For instance, a user can use a computer to **write a document**, **listen to music**, and **browse the internet** at the same time.
 
• It enables the computer to be used in various fields like **education**, **business**, **medicine**, and **engineering** by simply changing the **software or instructions**. ***Hence, this statement describes task flexibility rather than calculation speed.***
 
 
 
• **Accuracy:**
 
 
• **Accuracy** ensures that the computer performs calculations with **100% correctness**, provided the input data is correct. If a computer produces a wrong result, it is usually due to **human error** in data entry or **faulty programming**.
 
• This principle is known as **GIGO (Garbage In, Garbage Out)**. Computers do not make **mathematical mistakes** on their own because their internal logic is based on **binary electronic circuits**. ***Hence, this statement refers to the quality of the result, not the time taken.***
 
 
 
• **Automation:**
 
 
• **Automation** is the characteristic that allows a computer to perform a **series of tasks** without **human intervention** once the initial instructions (program) are given.
 
• It is widely used in **industrial manufacturing**, **automated emails**, and **operating systems** to manage background processes. ***Hence, this statement refers to self-execution capabilities.***
 
 
 
• **Diligence:**
 
 
• Unlike humans, computers do not suffer from **tiredness**, **boredom**, or **lack of concentration**. They can work for **hours or days** continuously and still maintain the **same speed and accuracy** as the first second.
 
• This makes them ideal for **repetitive tasks** in data processing and monitoring systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evolution of Speed:** The speed of computers has increased exponentially since the **first generation (1940s)**, which used **Vacuum Tubes** and processed thousands of instructions, to the **fifth generation**, which utilizes **Ultra Large Scale Integration (ULSI)** and **Artificial Intelligence**.
 
• **Clock Speed:** The **Clock Speed** of a computer's processor determines how many **cycles** it can execute per second. A **3.5 GHz** processor can perform **3.5 billion cycles** per second.
 
• **Storage Capacity:** Along with speed, a computer's ability to **store large volumes of data** in **Hard Disk Drives (HDD)** or **Solid State Drives (SSD)** in terms of **Terabytes (TB)** or **Petabytes (PB)** complements its calculating power by providing instant access to information.
 
• **Global Context:** Countries like the **USA**, **China**, and **Japan** lead in the development of **high-speed computing technology**, with India also contributing through its **National Supercomputing Mission (NSM)** and indigenous supercomputers like **PARAM Siddhi-AI**.
